newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Nov 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Nov 5.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- BT MERGER FUELS BID SPECULATION

The world of telecommunications is reported to be rife with rumours of possible takeovers and alliances in the wake of the announcement of a massive deal involving British Telecom and US carrier MCI. There are reports that France Telecom is looking to boost its presence in the Sprint alliance with Deutsche Telekom, while Cable & Wireless is also rumoured to be examining a possible alliance in international calls with Nynex. Observers are looking to see what the reaction will be from AT&T to these challenges to its domestic market.
-- ABF PROFITS RISE 15 PERCENT AS RETAILING AND FOOD REBOUND

Associated British Foods on Monday reported a rise in pre-tax profits for the year to September 4 to 430 million stg. The figures were boosted by higher prices as well as improvements made in the area of costs. Forecasts for the current year have been increased to 450 million stg thanks to the better than had been expected numbers. The company is reported to be planning further start-ups as well as overseas acquisitions as part of its diversification programme.
-- BRITISH BIOTECH CANCER DRUG DATA DISAPPOINT MARKET

There has been a disappointed market reaction to the latest set of data on trials of the British Biotech anti-cancer drug marimastat. The latest data on the drug did not cover the impact it had on the length of life of those using it, instead concentrating on the effect on the blood. However, the figures do reduce the chances that positive effects in patients are the result of a placebo effect. Shares in British Biotech fell on the news.
-- TALKS DEADLOCKED ON EMU BUDGET DISCIPLINE

German insistence that rigid rules be applied to budgetary discipline among countries participating in the process of Emu is reported to be presenting a major obstacle to an agreement being reached on the issue before the end of the year. While the forging of such a stability pact is not likely to delay the planned launch of a single currency, there are fears that it could undermine market confidence in the process.
-- MONEY SUPPLY SURGE POINTS TO STRONG SALES

The latest money supply figures for October indicate that the amount of cash circulating in the UK economy increased, indicating the strength of consumer spending. This, as well as figures showing increases in housebuilding as well as an expected rise in factory production, is likely to prompt the Bank of England to take a cautious approach to its assessment of the prognosis for inflation in a quarterly report to be published on Wednesday.
-- FEARS GROW OF EMU-INDUCED FLIGHT TO SWISS FRANC

A study for the Swiss economic ministry warns that the country might experience a surge in inflows of currency in the lead-up to European monetary union. The report suggests that measures, such as tougher monetary targets, be introduced to offset the effects of any flight towards the Swiss franc by nervous investors. The Swiss have grown increasingly concerned that uncertainty surrounding the single currency could cause investors to switch into hard currencies.
-- SWEDEN URGED TO DELAY EMU ENTRY

An independent study on behalf of the Swedish government has advised that the country avoid entering the single European currency at its start date in 1999, noting that the political and economic arguments favour a wait and see approach. There is a high level of opposition among the Swedish electorate to the euro. The panel that drew up the report, however, with the exception of one, were unanimous in their belief that Sweden should join the single currency at a later date.
-- VISA LAUNCHES NEW MULTI-FUNCTION CARD

Visa International in association with First National and Nedcor, both South African banks, has launched its first ever multi-function smartcard which will operate as a credit, debit and pre-pay card. The card contains a microchip and according to the company is the direction in which all such cards will evolve over the next 20 years. South Africa has seen smartcards develop at a faster pace because of the paucity of its telecoms system making standard transaction verification less practical.
-- HALIFAX PREDICTS 7 PERCENT HOUSE PRICE RISE

The Halifax has predicted that house prices in Britain will increase for this year at a rate of 7 percent in the wake of a sharp rise in prices last month when average costs for homes surged 1.6 percent. Although the Halifax does not expect this rate of increase to be repeated in the short-term, it did note that a general upward trend was to be expected. Meanwhile, the Department of the Environment has reported an increase in the level of construction, boosted by increasing sales.
-- HYDER SCRAPS 35 MILLION STG IBM COMPUTER PLAN

Hyder, owner of electricity company Swalec and Welsh Water, has abandoned plans to invest 35 million sterling in an IBM computer system that had been intended to allow the company to compete more effectively for electricity customers in 1998. The system, called Croseo, is reported to have failed to meet time and cost targets and is being dropped in favour of a system inherited by the company from Welsh Water. Sweb, another electricity company involved in the project is now reviewing its involvement.
